title: Signature Movement Cleaning Procedure
body:
Specifications

An original Signature cleaning procedure for Signature movements, with a documented strip order, a cleaning solution made for Signature brass and steel, and a reassembly checklist. It is labelled signature-original and is written for Signature movements, though its principles match standard practice.

Mechanism

Disassembly starts with letting down the power, weights removed and held, or the mainspring let down in controlled steps, and only then are the plates separated. Wheels are cleaned in the Signature solution, pivots are polished with pegwood and a fine file, and the plates are brushed and rinsed. Reassembly reverses the order, with each wheel checked for freedom before the plates are closed, and the checklist is signed off at each step.

Maintenance

Never clean a Signature movement with the power still on, and never use household cleaners or water without drying fully, because rust follows damp pivots. Photograph the movement before stripping it, so the order is certain on reassembly.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration cleaning also checks every pivot hole, tooth, and spring, and replaces worn parts before reassembly rather than after. Test the movement on a stand for a week before returning it to its case, and record the test in the service notes.

Tools

Signature cleaning solution, pegwood, pivot files, screwdrivers, camera, and clock oil.

title: Signature Oiling Schedule
body:
Specifications

An original Signature oiling schedule that lists every oil point on a Signature movement, the oil to use at each point, and the interval between oilings. It is labelled signature-original and is kept with the movement's service notes.

Mechanism

Oil is applied with a fine oiler to each pivot as it sits in its hole, so capillary action draws it in, and to each pallet impulse face, where the escape wheel teeth slide. Oil is used in tiny amounts: one drop per point, and nowhere else. Oil on the teeth, the suspension, the dial, or the case does no good and attracts dust, and over-oiling is worse than slight under-oiling, because excess oil creeps and carries dust into the pivots.

Maintenance

Oil only the points on the Signature schedule, one drop each, and never oil a movement that has not been cleaned, because new oil on old, dirty oil makes a grinding paste. Never use household oil or spray lubricants on a Signature movement.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration oiling follows a full cleaning, with each pivot checked for freedom first, and the oil points are ticked off on the schedule so the next service can see what was done. Test the rate for a week after oiling.

Tools

Clock oil, fine oilers, loupe, pegwood, and the Signature oiling schedule.

title: Signature Beat Setting Method
body:
Specifications

An original Signature beat setting method that uses a beat amplifier and a crutch bending gauge, with the beat error recorded before and after adjustment. It is labelled signature-original and is written for Signature longcase movements.

Mechanism

The pendulum hangs from its suspension, and the crutch fork pushes it through the anchor. If the crutch is bent slightly one way, the anchor releases one pallet early and the other late, so the ticks are uneven. The Signature method bends the crutch a fraction, measures the beat error, and repeats until the intervals match, rather than bending by ear alone.

Maintenance

Set the beat with the clock level and in its case position, because a clock set in beat on a bench may be out of beat when hung on a leaning wall. Never bend the crutch by force against the anchor, and never bend the pendulum rod to set the beat.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration beat setting follows cleaning and levelling, and it is checked at full swing and at low swing, because a beat even at full swing can be uneven as the swing falls. Record the beat error in the service notes.

Tools

Beat amplifier, Signature crutch gauge, spirit level, and screwdrivers.

title: Signature Bushing System
body:
Specifications

An original Signature bushing system using screw-in bushes of Signature brass, with a gauge that sets the bush depth and a reamer that finishes the bush to the pivot. It is labelled signature-original and is made for Signature plates.

Mechanism

A worn hole is reamed round and slightly larger, a Signature bush is screwed in to a set depth, and the bush is then reamed to fit the pivot with a small clearance, about two hundredths of a millimetre. The wheel must then sit at the correct depth with its neighbours, which is checked with a depthing tool before the plates are closed.

Maintenance

Check every pivot hole for wear before bushing, and bush only the holes that need it, because an unnecessary bush changes the wheel's position. Never force a bush in without reaming, because the plate cracks or the bush sits crooked.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration bushing uses bushes of Signature brass, reams them to the pivot with a smooth finish, and checks the depthing of every wheel pair after bushing. Test the movement for freedom before oiling.

Tools

Signature bushing tool, reamers, Signature bushes, depthing tool, and loupe.

title: Signature Suspension Replacement
body:
Specifications

An original Signature suspension replacement kit with springs in three thicknesses, matched to Signature pendulum weights, and a gauge that sets the spring length. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

The pendulum hangs from the suspension spring's lower block, and the spring flexes as the pendulum swings, so the pendulum's pivot is the spring itself, with almost no friction. The spring's length and thickness set the pendulum's rate, and the Signature kit's gauge lets the repairer choose the spring that matches the pendulum's weight, rather than guessing.

Maintenance

Handle a suspension spring by its blocks, never by the spring itself, because finger oil and bending weaken it. Check the spring for cracks under a loupe before fitting, and never straighten a kinked spring and reuse it.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration suspension uses a spring matched to the pendulum's weight, with the top block fixed firmly and the bottom block square to the rod. Test the swing for freedom and check the beat after fitting.

Tools

Signature suspension kit, loupe, screwdrivers, and a beat tester.

title: Signature Case Care Routine
body:
Specifications

An original Signature case care routine for Signature cases, with a wax made for Signature finishes and a cleaning cloth that does not shed fibres. It is labelled signature-original and is written for Signature mahogany, oak, and walnut cases.

Mechanism

Wood is cleaned with a soft, dry cloth, and only occasionally with the Signature wax, never with spray polish, which builds up and dulls the finish. Brass is cleaned with a soft cloth and a gentle cleaner, kept away from the dial and the movement. Glass is cleaned with a soft cloth and a little glass cleaner, kept away from the dial's paint. The case must stand level, out of direct sunlight, and away from radiators and damp walls.

Maintenance

Never use water on a Signature case, never spray polish near the dial, and never move a longcase clock with its weights and pendulum still in place. Always remove the weights and pendulum before moving the case, even across a room.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration case repair matches the wood and finish, repairs veneer with matching veneer, and re-lacquers only the repaired area where possible, so the case keeps its age and character. Record the finish used.

Tools

Soft cloths, Signature wax, brass cleaner, glass cleaner, and screwdrivers.

title: Signature Movement Safety Code
body:
Specifications

An original Signature safety code for handling Signature movements, covering mainspring let-down, weight removal, and eye protection, and printed on the inside of every Signature movement's job card. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

A mainspring stores a large amount of energy in its barrel, and if it is released suddenly it can spin the barrel, break teeth, and cut hands. Weights, typically several kilograms each on a longcase clock, hang on lines or chains, and if a line breaks or a weight is lifted carelessly, the weight falls and the case is damaged. The Signature code requires weights removed first and supported as they come down, and a mainspring let down in small, controlled steps with a let-down tool, never by hand alone.

Maintenance

Never open a Signature movement with the power on, never let a mainspring down by holding the barrel by hand, and never stand under a weight as it is removed. Wear eye protection when working on a mainspring barrel, and keep hands clear of the barrel's path.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature workshop keeps a let-down tool, a mainspring winder, and a weight cradle, and it trains every worker in power let-down before they touch a movement. Record the power state on the job card before stripping begins.

Tools

Let-down tool, mainspring winder, weight cradle, eye protection, and gloves.

title: Signature Weight Drive Service
body:
Specifications

An original Signature weight drive service for Signature eight-day movements, with a line gauge that checks gut lines and a weight scale that matches each weight to its train. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

Winding raises the weights, and as they fall they turn the barrel, which drives the centre wheel and the rest of the going train. The lines must run true on their drums and pulleys, and the weights must hang free without touching the case or each other. The strike and chime trains have their own weights, and each weight must be matched to its train by the Signature scale.

Maintenance

Check the lines for fraying at every service, and replace a frayed line before it breaks, because a falling weight damages the case and the movement. Keep the pulleys clean and oiled, and never swap the weights between trains.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration weight service replaces worn lines with the correct gut or cable, checks the drums for grooves, and matches each weight to its train. Test the run time for a full week after service.

Tools

Gut lines or cable, pulleys, Signature weight scale, screwdrivers, and clock oil.

title: Signature Mainspring Handling
body:
Specifications

An original Signature mainspring handling procedure with a barrel opener and a winder sized for Signature barrels, and a spring gauge that checks a spring's strength before fitting. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

The spring is wound in its barrel, and its energy drives the barrel's teeth, which drive the going train. Letting it down means holding the barrel with a let-down tool and releasing the click a fraction at a time, so the spring unwinds slowly. Removing it means opening the barrel and lifting the spring out with a winder, and rewinding means winding it back in with the same tool, keeping the coils even.

Maintenance

Never let a Signature mainspring down by hand, never open a barrel without holding the spring, and never reuse a spring with a cracked or set coil, because it will break in service and damage the train. Wear eye protection for all mainspring work.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration mainspring service checks the spring for set, cracks, and rust, replaces a faulty spring with one of the same strength and size, and records the spring's dimensions. Test the power at the escape wheel after fitting, before closing the movement.

Tools

Let-down tool, Signature mainspring winder, barrel opener, eye protection, and gloves.

title: Signature Pendulum Regulation
body:
Specifications

An original Signature pendulum regulation method using a rating nut with a graduated dial, so each turn's effect on the rate can be read off and recorded. It is labelled signature-original and is made for Signature seconds pendulums.

Mechanism

The rating nut turns on a threaded rod under the bob, and one full turn typically changes the rate by about ten seconds a day on a seconds pendulum, though the exact figure varies by movement. The Signature graduated dial lets the repairer record the nut's position before and after each adjustment, so the regulation can be undone exactly if it overshoots.

Maintenance

Regulate only after the clock is clean, oiled, in beat, and level, because regulating a dirty or out-of-beat clock chases a moving target. Never turn the rating nut by large amounts at once, and never regulate by bending the pendulum rod.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration regulation records the rate before and after each nut turn, and it checks the rate at the same time of day, because temperature changes the pendulum's length and the rate with it.

Tools

Signature rating nut dial, timing machine, and a rate log.

title: Signature Dial and Hand Care
body:
Specifications

An original Signature dial and hand care routine for Signature dials, with a soft brush that does not shed and a hand setter that sets hands without bending them. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

The dial is cleaned with a soft, dry brush, and only very gently, because paint flakes if it is rubbed or wetted. Hands are cleaned separately, with a soft cloth, and refitted with their collets square and their clearance set so they do not touch each other or the dial. The hands must be set so the hour hand points correctly at each hour, which is checked by the strike.

Maintenance

Never use water or cleaner on a painted Signature dial, never bend a hand to correct a strike error, and never polish a silvered dial with abrasive, because the silvering is thin and will wear through. A dial with flaking paint should be left alone and shown to a specialist.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration dial repair consolidates flaking paint, retouches only where the loss is certain, and matches the original colours, so the dial keeps its age. Record the dial's condition with photographs before any work.

Tools

Soft brushes, hand puller, Signature hand setter, loupe, and camera.

title: Signature Strike Troubleshooting
body:
Specifications

An original Signature strike troubleshooting chart that tests the going train, the strike train, and the chime train in order, with the fault at each hour recorded on the chart. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

Test the going train first, then the strike train alone, then the chime train alone, counting the blows at every hour. A strike that counts correctly at three but fails at twelve points to a worn snail step or a worn count-wheel notch at twelve. A chime that plays the wrong quarter points to a barrel one step out or a selector fault. A strike that lags points to a warning fault.

Maintenance

Never bend a rack, a count wheel, or a selector lever to cure a fault without finding the worn part first, because bending hides the fault and creates a new one. Never adjust the hands to correct a strike count on a rack-and-snail clock, because the snail is driven by the hands.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration troubleshooting records the fault at every hour, the train at fault, and the part replaced or adjusted, so the next service can see the history. Test the full twelve hours, twice, before returning the clock.

Tools

Signature troubleshooting chart, warning lever gauge, screwdrivers, and a beat tester.

title: Signature Pivot Polishing
body:
Specifications

An original Signature pivot polishing method using a burnisher with a Signature profile, which hardens and polishes a pivot without removing much metal. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

The pivot is held in a lathe or a pivot polisher and smoothed with a fine file, then with the Signature burnisher, which hardens and polishes the surface. The pivot must stay round and straight, and its diameter must not be reduced by more than a few hundredths of a millimetre, or it will be loose in its hole and need bushing.

Maintenance

Never polish a pivot with coarse abrasive, never polish a pivot that is already undersize, and never polish a pivot without checking its hole, because a polished pivot in a worn hole still runs badly. Check the pivot for straightness before and after polishing.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration pivot polish records the pivot's diameter before and after, and it checks the depthing after polishing, because a thinner pivot sits differently in its hole. Test the wheel for freedom before oiling.

Tools

Signature pivot polisher, fine files, Signature burnisher, micrometer, and loupe.

title: Signature Wear Inspection
body:
Specifications

An original Signature wear inspection that measures depthing and endshake for every wheel pair and records them on a Signature inspection sheet. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

Depthing is checked with a depthing tool, which holds two wheels at their correct centres and shows whether the teeth mesh too deeply, too shallowly, or correctly. Endshake is checked by lifting each wheel along its arbor and feeling the small movement, which should be present but not excessive. Too little endshake binds the wheel, and too much lets it wander and wear its pivots unevenly.

Maintenance

Check depthing and endshake after any bushing or pivot work, because both change the wheel's position. Never close the plates without checking every wheel pair, because a depthing fault found after closing means stripping the movement again.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration inspection records the depthing and endshake of every wheel pair, and it corrects faults by bushing, pivot work, or plate work, in that order. Test the movement for freedom before oiling.

Tools

Depthing tool, endshake gauge, loupe, and the Signature inspection sheet.

title: Signature Reassembly and Test
body:
Specifications

An original Signature reassembly and test procedure with a checklist for every wheel's freedom, the beat setting, and a week-long test stand run. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

The wheels are fitted in order, the plates are closed, and each wheel is checked for freedom by turning it by hand. The escapement is fitted, the beat is set, and the movement is run on a test stand for at least a week, with its rate, beat, and strike counted daily. Only when the movement runs steadily for a week is it returned to its case and its pendulum fitted.

Maintenance

Never return a Signature movement to its case after a bench test of an hour, because faults in rate and strike show over days, not hours. Never fit the pendulum before the beat is set, because the pendulum's weight hides a beat fault.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration reassembly records the test week's rate and beat daily, and it notes any adjustment made during the week, so the owner can see the movement's true performance. Test the strike at every hour during the test week.

Tools

Test stand, beat tester, timing machine, and a rate log.

title: Signature Storage and Environment
body:
Specifications

An original Signature storage and environment guide for Signature clocks, with a dust cover, a weight cradle, and a pendulum packing case made for Signature longcase clocks. It is labelled signature-original.

Mechanism

A clock in storage should have its weights removed, its pendulum removed and packed separately, its movement covered against dust, and its case kept upright, level, and out of direct sunlight. The room should be dry, with stable temperature, because damp rusts pivots and swells wood, and heat dries wood and cracks veneer. A running clock should also stand level, out of sunlight, and away from radiators, because a leaning clock runs out of beat and a hot clock runs fast as its pendulum expands.

Maintenance

Never store a Signature clock with its weights hanging, never lay a longcase clock on its side with its movement in place, and never store a clock in a damp garage or attic. Check a stored clock every few months for damp and dust, and wind a stored spring-driven clock occasionally so its spring does not set.

Build and restoration guidance

A Signature restoration storage plan records the clock's condition when stored, the weights and pendulum removed, and the room's conditions, so the clock can be returned to service with a known history. Inspect the movement before running a clock that has been stored for a year or more.

Tools

Signature dust cover, weight cradle, pendulum packing, hygrometer, and a spirit level.
